subject: Forensic log review for recent service disruption — summary and customer-facing statement
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finservco.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finservco.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident on 2027-02-11 — request for log integrity check

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the update this morning. Our security team is asking for a concise statement that FinServ Co can include in our internal post-incident review: specifically, did Redwood observe any indication of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access during the disruption window (2027-02-11T22:30Z to 2027-02-12T01:10Z)?

If possible, can you provide: 1) a short customer-facing statement we can attach to our incident summary, and 2) the list of log samples or evidence you reviewed (file names/sha256) so our SOC can cross-check?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emma Liu
Head of Security Operations
FinServ Co

---
Original message: thanks for keeping us posted earlier — appreciate the collaboration on this one."

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finservco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident on 2027-02-11 — request for log integrity check

Emma —

Short answer up front: we have not found evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized access tied to the incident window. That said, my team is completing a forensic sweep and will provide the detailed artifact list and a summarized statement you can share with your auditors by Monday.

What we'll provide:
- A one-paragraph customer-facing statement you can paste into your post-incident notes.
- A signed hash list (sha256) of the log samples we examined.
- A short description of the scope and methods used (query samples, selectors, and timeframe).

Mina and Markus are leading the log review — copying them to confirm ETA and attachments.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 07:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Forensic log review — preliminary findings and artifacts

Team —

Attached: forensic_log_sample_20270212.zip (contains anonymized log slices and request ids), forensic_summary_20270214.pdf (technical summary and signed hash list).

Summary (executive):
- Scope: evaluated application and network logs for the affected serving cluster (svc-redwood-03) between 2027-02-11T22:15Z and 2027-02-12T02:00Z, plus supporting control-plane audit logs.
- Findings: no patterns indicating data exfiltration, no unusual outbound transfers, and no lateral authentication from unknown principals. All access during the window aligns with expected service accounts and customer request traffic.
- Sampling: we validated a stratified sample of 4,000 request traces (see attested file) and computed SHA256 hashes for each sample file:
  - forensic_log_sample_20270212_part1.gz — sha256: a3f1d5c...
  - forensic_log_sample_20270212_part2.gz — sha256: 4b8c9f2...
  - control_plane_audit_20270212.gz — sha256: f9e7b11...

Caveats and next steps:
- We could not reconstruct two truncated traces due to collection buffering; we flagged those for further review and they are included in the supplemental index. Neither trace contains customer payloads based on metadata.
- We will run a second-pass correlation against cache eviction events and report back if anything changes (expected completion: 2027-02-14 14:00Z PST).

If the team signs off on the language below, Rafael can send the customer-facing statement.

Proposed customer-facing statement (technical summary removed):
"Redwood completed a forensic review of service and audit logs for the affected cluster and found no evidence of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access during the incident window. A stratified sample of request traces and control-plane audit logs were reviewed; no anomalous outbound transfers or access from unknown principals were observed. Redwood will continue an extended correlation pass and will notify you if any further findings emerge."

-Markus
Senior Reliability Engineer

(Attachments: forensic_log_sample_20270212.zip, forensic_summary_20270214.pdf)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finservco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, security@finservco.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Forensic log review for recent service disruption — summary and customer-facing statement

Emma —

Following up with our final, customer-ready statement and attached evidence. Please find the short statement below and the attached artifact bundle (forensic_summary_20270214.pdf includes the signed hash list).

Customer-facing statement (for your post-incident notes):
"Redwood completed a forensic review of service and audit logs covering the incident window on 2027-02-11. Based on a stratified review of request traces and control-plane audit logs, Redwood did not observe any evidence of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access related to the incident. We will continue an extended correlation pass across cache and network telemetry and will notify FinServ Co immediately if any new findings emerge."

Artifacts provided (attached):
- forensic_summary_20270214.pdf — technical summary and sha256 list for provided samples
- forensic_log_sample_20270212.zip — anonymized log slices (sampled request ids)

If your SOC needs any additional slices, or hashed identifiers that tie directly to your request ids, let us know the format and we'll provide them under NDA as required.

Thanks for working through this with us — we know these reviews are important to close the loop.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0139
